old: It may echo a small chime, the kind of noise something makes when struck just right.
Some say it's a dressed-up version of a word for that ringing sound, first written down in the 1920s.
It might share a thread with "stingo," though no one's entirely sure how tightly they're tied.
clues: This crowd-pleasing game of chance may owe its name to someone imitating the ring of a bell, a sound echoed in the triumphant shout that ends each round.
Unlike a lottery or keno, each player daubs numbers on their own grid card as a caller draws them, racing to complete a row first in church halls everywhere.
People also cry it as an exclamation meaning "Exactly, that's it!" when something clicks into place. It may be linked to the old word "stingo," though that connection is uncertain.
